bio: Moataz Bellah Asem Ata Abu Sree’ is a rising Egyptian taekwondo sensation who has rocketed to the top of the World Taekwondo rankings before his 21st birthday. Specialising in the men’s −54 kg kyorugi division, he became world No. 1 in September 2025 with 124.56 ranking points after a string of podium finishes on three continents. Since bursting onto the senior scene in 2022 with youth-level golds at the Arab Cup and Fujairah Open, Abu Sree’ has collected titles across Africa, Oceania and Europe. His 2024 season was highlighted by a gold medal at the African Games in Accra and back-to-back victories at the Malabo Open and WT President’s Cup-Africa. Maintaining that momentum, he opened 2025 with gold at the President’s Cup-Africa, added silver medals at the Australian and German Opens, and struck gold again at the President’s Cup-Oceania. A regular member of Egypt’s national team, he also represented his university at the Rhine-Ruhr 2025 FISU World University Games. According to TaekwondoData, he owns a 17-9 career record in recorded international bouts, winning 65 percent of his fights. Abu Sree’s rapid ascent and fearless style have established him as one of Africa’s brightest hopes for the Paris 2028 Olympic cycle.

playersStory:
Born on 18 August 2005, Moataz Bellah Asem Ata Abu Sree’ first stepped onto the mats at a local club in Cairo as a hyperactive ten-year-old looking for an outlet. Early coaches quickly noticed his explosive kicking ability and unusually keen tactical awareness. By 16 he was dominating regional cadet events; a double gold haul at the 2022 Arab Cup and Fujairah Open marked his transition from promising youth to legitimate international prospect.

2023 became his breakthrough season at senior level. Competing against older, stronger athletes, he claimed his first G-level senior title at the WT President’s Cup-Africa in Cairo, then backed it up with silvers at the Senegal and Beirut Opens and bronze at the African Championships. Each tournament sharpened his ring craft, especially his counter-back-kick that has become a signature weapon.

The real turning point arrived in March 2024 when he captured African Games gold in Accra. Fighting five matches in one day, he overcame leg cramps in the semifinal before edging Nigeria’s Ahmad Rawy in a tense final. The triumph convinced him he could contend for Olympic qualification. Later that year he swept the Malabo Open and repeated as President’s Cup-Africa champion, propelling him into the world top ten.

In 2025 Abu Sree’ tested himself far from home. A bronze at the Arab Cup and a gutsy fifth-place finish at the Charlotte Grand Prix Challenge were followed by an Oceania tour where he struck gold at the President’s Cup-Oceania and silver at the Australian Open. Returning to Europe, he pushed Turkey’s Furkan Camoglu to the limit before settling for silver at the German Open. Those performances vaulted him to World No. 1 in M-54 kg and No. 3 on the Olympic M-58 kg list. Still only 20, the Egyptian prodigy balances national-team camps with university studies and is already being hailed by the Egyptian Taekwondo Federation as the natural successor to Olympic medallist Seif Eissa. With Paris 2028 qualification events on the horizon, Abu Sree’ is determined to translate ranking points into global podiums while inspiring the next generation of Egyptian fighters.
